analyses.change: Login rate limiting and registration input validation
analyses.observed_change: taskflow/security/rate_limiter.py was added: RateLimiter class with MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, LOCKOUT_SECONDS=300 (5 minutes); record_failure(key) appends time.monotonic() timestamps; is_locked(key) returns True when recent failure count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS; clear(key) removes the key on successful login; module-level singleton rate_limiter. taskflow/api/auth.py was modified (+26 lines, -1 line): rate_limiter imported; login() now calls is_locked() before authentication and returns HTTP 429 with message 'Too many failed attempts — try again later' when locked; record_failure() called on PermissionError; clear() called on success. register() gained length validation: username > 64 chars returns 422, email > 254 chars returns 422, password > 128 chars returns 422, password < 8 chars returns 422 with message 'password must be at least 8 characters'. README.md updated with two bullet points documenting the rate limiting and input validation as user-facing features.
analyses.stated_intent: The commit message states: 'security: add login rate limiter (max 5 attempts / 5 min) and input length validation on registration'. The 'security:' prefix classifies this explicitly as a security change. The message names the specific policy: 5 attempts per 5 minutes. README.md explicitly documents 'Token-based authentication with brute-force rate limiting' and 'Input validation on all endpoints' as features — this is a repository-observable statement of what was intended to be user-visible.
analyses.evidence_based_inference: [INFERENCE] The parameter values (MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, LOCKOUT_SECONDS=300) are consistent with commonly documented brute-force mitigation thresholds, but the repository contains no document, comment, or reference that explains why these specific values were chosen. The input length limits (64 / 254 / 128) correspond to conventional web field limits — 254 characters matches the RFC 5321 maximum email address length — suggesting awareness of standards, but no reference to any RFC or standard appears in the code or commit. The fact that this commit arrives as the final commit in the repository, after the test suite, is consistent with security hardening being a late-stage concern, but the repository does not state this ordering was deliberate. The README update listing security features suggests this was considered a user-visible, documentable capability rather than an internal implementation detail.
analyses.unknown: The repository contains no evidence explaining: (1) what triggered the security hardening — no vulnerability report, no security review note, and no external reference is present; (2) why the rate limiter is in-memory rather than persistent — an in-memory rate limiter does not survive server restarts, but no comment acknowledges this limitation; (3) why 5 attempts / 5 minutes specifically; (4) why input validation was not added when the register() endpoint was first written in c5040fb; (5) whether the security changes were added in response to a specific concern or as a proactive measure — insufficient repository evidence to determine this.

evidence.reason: All changes in this commit. Diff of rate_limiter.py shows MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 and LOCKOUT_SECONDS=300 constants. Diff of auth.py shows 429 response and is_locked() integration. README diff shows explicit security feature documentation.
